reason: This passage (Exodus 11-12 in the Masoretic text) describes the tenth plague and the Exodus from Egypt. While it contains references to cries and expressions of fear by Egyptians (וַתְּהִי צְעָקָה גְדֹלָה בְּמִצְרַיִם - 'there was a great cry in Egypt'; כִּי אָמְרוּ כֻּלָּנוּ מֵתִים - 'for they said, We be all dead men'), the text does not depict Yahweh's anger being triggered by people voicing their opinions and feelings. Rather, Yahweh's anger is already established through the announcement and execution of the plague itself. The people's vocalizations shown here are reactions to the plague's devastation, not causes of Yahweh's anger. The passage focuses on divine action and the Exodus narrative, not on Yahweh responding with anger to complaint or opinion-voicing.
